summary: People keep circling "cinema of the absurd" because this turns a police-power joke into a sharp, eerie power game. It is dry, sly, and much funnier than its premise sounds.
good_pick_if: You want a sharp satire that keeps its cool while it gets stranger.
maybe_skip_if: You want a straightforward police procedural or comfort watch.

summary: People still quote "a good love scene should be about something else besides love" because the dialogue has bite and the romance feels bruised. It is sharp, volatile, and forever a little off-balance.
good_pick_if: You want a romantic thriller with great lines and a tense mood.
maybe_skip_if: You want a gentle love story or characters you can relax around.

summary: People love how it is "a situation" for Cary Grant, because the movie never stops moving once the chase starts. It is sleek, witty, and built for pure suspense with just enough romance and comedy to keep it light on its feet.

maybe_skip_if: You want something slow, dark, or psychologically heavy.

summary: People keep calling it "a sociological experiment" because the stripped-back staging makes every shift in power feel exposed. It is cold, confrontational, and built to make a room talk afterward.
good_pick_if: You want a bold, formal experiment that makes its point through design.
maybe_skip_if: You want naturalistic sets or an easy emotional release.

summary: People call it "silly comedy" in the same breath as horror because the movie is all camp, sabotage, and sour old-Hollywood energy. It is theatrical, nasty, and weirdly hard to stop watching.
good_pick_if: You want melodrama with a mean streak and big performances.
maybe_skip_if: You want subtlety or a clean, comforting tone.

summary: People call it "a blueprint movie for thrillers to come," and that is exactly the pull: everything feels engineered for dread. It is elegant, tense, and mean in the most satisfying way.

maybe_skip_if: You want a relaxed pace or no-nonsense answers.
